chunks: So extinguish what is hidden in your hearts from the fires of tribalism, and the hatreds of ignorance.
And that zeal is only in the Muslim from the flittings of Satan, his haughtiness, his mischief, and his whisperings.
And adopt the placing of humility over your heads, and casting off self-pride under your feet, and removing arrogance from your necks.
And take humility as a weapon between you and your enemy, Iblis, and his forces, for he has from every nation fighters and helpers, footmen and horsemen.

And do not be like the one who feigned superiority over the son of his mother, without any distinction Allah had placed in him, except what greatness attached to himself from the enmity of envy, and what zeal kindled in his heart from the fire of anger, and Satan blew into his nose from the wind of arrogance.
Which Allah caused him to follow with remorse, and made him responsible for the sins of the killers until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: How does one combat the hidden vices of arrogance and tribalism according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) diagnoses the root of social discord as 'nasab' (tribal pride) and 'kibr' (arrogance), attributing them to Satan's whispers rather than genuine merit. He employs the metaphor of the arrogant man who killed his servant to illustrate how unchecked vanity leads to eternal guilt, urging believers to strip themselves of pride and adopt humility as a spiritual armor against Iblis's legion.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You should therefore put out the fires of haughtiness and the flames of intolerance that are hidden in your hearts.
This vanity can exist in a Muslim only by the machinations of Satan, his haughtiness, mischief and whisperings.
Make up your mind to have humility over your heads, to trample self-pride under your feet and to cast off vanity from your necks.
Adopt humility as the weapon between you and your enemy, Satan and his forces.

He certainly has, from every people, fighters, helpers, footmen and horsemen. Do not be like him who feigned superiority over the son of his own mother without any distinction given to him by Allāh except the feeling of envy which his feeling of greatness created in him and the fire of anger that vanity kindled in his heart. Satan blew into his nose his own vanity,
after which Allāh gave him remorse and made him responsible for the sins of all killers up to the Day of Judgement.
